sections.title: باب 2 — متن (132)

paras.text: In this hadith the excellence of the merchant who deals gently with one in hardship is mentioned. In the economic system of Islam such teachings have been given which are no less than glad tidings for the needy, the destitute, widows, orphans and helpless people. Helping the poverty-stricken through qard-e-hasanah (benevolent loans), sadaqah and khayrat, zakat, and the teachings of forgiving loans — these Islamic teachings are such principles, by acting upon which poverty can be ended from society, and deprived classes can get the opportunity to stand on their own feet.

paras.pashto: په دې حدیث کې د هغه سوداګر د فضیلت یادونه ده چې له تنګلاسي سره نرمي کوي. د اسلام په اقتصادي نظام کې داسې لارښوونې شوې چې د اړو، مسکینانو، کونډو، یتیمانو او بې‌سرپرسته خلکو لپاره له زېري کمې نه دي. د قرض حسنه له لارې د بېوزلو خلکو مرسته، صدقه او خیرات، زکات او د پور بښلو اسلامي لارښوونې داسې اصول دي چې پر هغو په عمل له ټولنې بېوزلي ختمېدای شي، او بې‌برخې طبقې د خپلو پښو د درېدو فرصت ومومي.

paras.text: The Noble Prophet ﷺ has given heart-refreshing glad tidings to such a merchant who, seeing some poverty-stricken person in hardship, or while dealing with him, tells his companion to forgive him, that is, give him something free of charge; and if he is a debtor, then forgive his loan; it is possible that by the alms of this deed Allah the Exalted forgives us too. paras.urdu: نبی کریم صلی اللہ علیہ وآلہٖ وسلم نے ایسے تاجر کو مژدۂ جانفزا سنایا ہے جو کسی مفلوک الحال تنگ دست کو دیکھ کر یا اس سے لین دین کرتے ہوئے اپنے ساتھی سے کہتا ہے کہ اسے معاف کر دو یعنی اسے کوئی چیز مفت میں دے دو اور اگر وہ مقروض ہے تو اس کا قرض معاف کر دو۔ ممکن ہے اللہ تعالیٰ اس عمل کے صدقے ہمیں بھی معاف کر دے۔ اللہ تعالیٰ ایسے شخص سے خوش ہو جاتا ہے جو اس کے کسی غریب اور مفلس بندے سے نرمی کا معاملہ فرماتا ہے۔
paras.pashto: نبي کریم ﷺ داسې سوداګر ته زړه‌راښکونکی زېری ورکړی چې کوم بېوزله تنګلاسی ویني یا ورسره راکړه ورکړه کوي، او خپل ملګري ته وايي چې وبښه یې، یعنې کوم شی ورته وړیا ورکړه، او که پوروړی وي، پور یې وبښه؛ کېدای شي الله تعالی د دې عمل په صدقه موږ هم وبښي. الله تعالی له داسې چا خوشالېږي چې د هغه له کوم غریب او بېوزله بنده سره نرم چلند کوي.

paras.text: We should show special sympathy with the poor in mutual dealings, and create ease for them, so that Allah the Exalted becomes pleased with us and forgives us.
paras.urdu: ہمیں چاہیے کہ باہمی لین دین میں غریبوں کے ساتھ خاص ہمدردی کریں۔ ان کے لیے آسانیاں پیدا کریں تاکہ اللہ تعالیٰ ہم سے خوش ہو جائے اور ہمیں بخش دے۔
paras.pashto: موږ باید په متقابله راکړه ورکړه کې له غریبانو سره ځانګړې همدردي وکړو، او د هغوی لپاره اسانتیاوې پیدا کړو، تر څو الله تعالی له موږ خوشاله شي او موږ وبښي.

Explanation

In this hadith the excellence of the merchant who deals gently with one in hardship is mentioned. In the economic system of Islam such teachings have been given which are no less than glad tidings for the needy, the destitute, widows, orphans and helpless people. Helping the poverty-stricken through qard-e-hasanah (benevolent loans), sadaqah and khayrat, zakat, and the teachings of forgiving loans — these Islamic teachings are such principles, by acting upon which poverty can be ended from society, and deprived classes can get the opportunity to stand on their own feet.

The Noble Prophet ﷺ has given heart-refreshing glad tidings to such a merchant who, seeing some poverty-stricken person in hardship, or while dealing with him, tells his companion to forgive him, that is, give him something free of charge; and if he is a debtor, then forgive his loan; it is possible that by the alms of this deed Allah the Exalted forgives us too. Allah the Exalted becomes pleased with such a person who deals gently with some poor and destitute servant of His.

sections.title: باب 2 — متن (133)

paras.text: Translation: Nu'man bin Bashir says: I heard the Noble Prophet ﷺ saying: "The lawful too is clear and the unlawful too is clear, and between these two are doubtful things which many people do not know. So whoever saved himself from these doubtful things saved his religion and his honour, and whoever fell into them is like that herdsman who grazes his herd around the pasture; it may be that it enters that pasture. Indeed, every king has a pasture, and the pasture of Allah is the things He has made unlawful. Translation: Nu'man bin Bashir says: I heard the Noble Prophet ﷺ saying: "The lawful too is clear and the unlawful too is clear, and between these two are doubtful things which many people do not know. So whoever saved himself from these doubtful things saved his religion and his honour, and whoever fell into them is like that herdsman who grazes his herd around the pasture; it may be that it enters that pasture. Indeed, every king has a pasture, and the pasture of Allah is the things He has made unlawful. Indeed, in the body there is a piece; when it remains sound, the whole body remains sound, and when it becomes corrupt, the whole body becomes corrupt. Indeed, that is the heart."

Explanation

In this blessed hadith the Noble Prophet ﷺ has told such a formula for testing the unlawful and the lawful, that is, things permissible and impermissible according to the Shari'ah, by using which we can not only attain success in this worldly life but can also be blessed with success in the Hereafter.

The Noble Prophet ﷺ said that the lawful and the unlawful are entirely clear; some things are such too which are between them; they are called doubtful (mutashabihat). About whatever thing doubt and suspicion arise, so that it is not known whether it is permissible or impermissible, then avoiding such things is necessary. In this regard his ﷺ saying is that Allah the Exalted has placed in the side of every person a heart which at once informs about doubtful things. If someone does not listen to the voice of the heart, that is, puts the voice of conscience behind his back, then he goes on sinking into the swamp of sins, and a time comes when he is not even able to distinguish lawful and unlawful. That is why it was said: avoid things that cast into doubt and suspicion, and keep your hearts well clean, so that it keeps informing you that such-and-such thing is right and such-and-such thing is wrong. May Allah the Exalted protect our hearts and grant us the ability to respond to the voice of conscience.
